stem: A team wants a device that not only detects known exploit traffic but can also block it inline before it reaches servers. Which control BEST fits?

options.rationale: An IPS sits inline and can actively block malicious traffic, making it a preventive control, unlike a passive IDS.
An IDS is passive and only alerts; it does not block traffic inline.
A honeypot is a decoy for detection and study, not an inline blocking mechanism.
A SIEM correlates and alerts on log data but does not block traffic inline.

stem: A login page displays a banner stating that unauthorized access is prohibited and monitored. This control is BEST classified as which type?

options.rationale: A warning banner discourages a would-be attacker before acting, which is the definition of a deterrent control.
A banner does not technically stop access; it only discourages, so it is deterrent rather than preventive.
A banner does not remediate or restore after an event, so it is not corrective.
A banner does not identify that an event occurred; it discourages beforehand.

stem: An organization wants to prevent unknown, never-before-seen malware from executing on endpoints. Which approach is BEST suited to this goal?

options.text: Application allowlisting that permits only approved software and denies everything else
options.rationale: Deny-by-default allowlisting blocks any unapproved binary, including unknown malware, without needing a prior signature.

options.text: Blocklisting that blocks only known-bad files
options.rationale: Blocklisting permits by default and cannot block malware it has never seen, leaving unknown threats able to run.

options.text: Relying solely on user awareness training
options.rationale: Training helps but does not technically prevent unknown malware from executing.
Disabling a firewall reduces protection and does nothing to prevent malware execution.

stem: A security team deploys a decoy server in a segmented network with no legitimate business purpose. What is the PRIMARY function of this system?

options.text: To detect and study attacker activity, since any interaction with it is inherently suspicious
options.rationale: A honeypot attracts and observes attackers; because no legitimate use exists, interactions are high-fidelity detective signals.

options.text: To block all inbound attacks at the perimeter
options.rationale: A honeypot does not block traffic; it lures and observes rather than prevents.

options.text: To serve production traffic for real users
options.rationale: A honeypot has no legitimate business role; it is purely a decoy.
A honeypot is not a backup mechanism; that is a corrective/recovery control.

stem: Before delivering email attachments to users, a company wants to safely observe how suspicious files behave. Which technique BEST accomplishes this?

options.text: Detonating the files in an isolated sandbox to observe behavior
options.rationale: Sandboxing runs suspicious code in isolation so its behavior can be analyzed without endangering production systems.

options.text: Opening the attachments directly on a user's workstation
options.rationale: Opening on a real workstation risks infecting production systems, the opposite of safe analysis.
Blanket deletion prevents legitimate business email and does not analyze behavior.

options.text: Forwarding attachments to all users to crowdsource review
options.rationale: Distributing suspicious files broadly increases risk rather than safely analyzing them.

stem: After a ransomware attack encrypts files, the team restores the data from clean backups. Restoring from backup is BEST classified as which type of control?

options.rationale: Restoring systems/data after an incident remediates the damage, which is a corrective (recovery) control.
A deterrent discourages an attack beforehand; restoring backups happens after the event.
Detective controls identify an event; restoring data does not detect, it repairs.
Preventive controls stop an action; restoring backups occurs after the damage is done.

stem: An IDS must catch novel attacks that have no existing signature. Which detection method is BEST suited to identifying previously unseen threats?

options.text: Anomaly/behavior-based detection that flags deviations from a normal baseline
options.rationale: Anomaly detection can flag never-before-seen activity by comparing against normal behavior, unlike signature matching.
Signature-based detection can only catch attacks that match existing signatures, missing truly novel threats.

options.text: A static deny list of known bad IP addresses
options.rationale: A static block list only stops known-bad sources, not novel attack behaviors.

options.text: Disabling detection to reduce false positives
options.rationale: Disabling detection removes the capability entirely and detects nothing.

stem: A firewall that blocks traffic to unauthorized ports is primarily which type of control?

options.rationale: By stopping unwanted traffic from reaching a system, a firewall prevents the unwanted action, making it preventive.
A firewall stops traffic beforehand; it does not remediate after an event.
While firewalls log, their primary blocking function is preventive, not merely detective.
A firewall actively blocks rather than merely discouraging, so its primary function is preventive.

stem: A SOC subscribes to a feed of current adversary indicators to keep its detection rules and IPS signatures up to date. This feed is BEST described as what?

options.text: Threat intelligence used to enrich and tune detective and preventive controls
options.rationale: Threat intelligence supplies current indicators and tactics that keep detection and prevention controls effective against active threats.
A threat feed provides adversary knowledge, not data backup or recovery.
Threat intelligence is informational; it is unrelated to physical entry control.
Threat feeds do not manage account provisioning.

stem: An architect layers a firewall, allowlisting, an IDS, and backups so that failure of one control is caught or mitigated by another. This design MOST directly reflects which principle?

options.rationale: Layering preventive, detective, and corrective controls so no single failure is catastrophic is the essence of defense in depth.
This is the opposite; relying on one control is what defense in depth avoids.
Obscurity is hiding details, not layering functional controls.
Least privilege limits access rights; it does not describe layering multiple control functions.

stem: A device is connected to a monitoring span port and generates alerts on suspicious traffic but cannot stop it. This device is MOST accurately which of the following?

options.rationale: Being on a span port and only alerting, without the ability to block, describes a passive, detective IDS.
An IPS is inline and can block; a span-port, alert-only device is not an IPS.
A firewall enforces access rules inline; the described device only monitors and alerts.
A load balancer distributes traffic and is unrelated to intrusion detection.

stem: An IDS alert notifies analysts that a suspicious scan occurred on the network. Detecting and alerting on this activity is BEST classified as which control type?

options.rationale: Identifying and signaling that an event occurred is the defining role of a detective control.
The IDS did not stop the scan; it only detected it, so it is detective, not preventive.
A deterrent discourages beforehand; the IDS reports after activity happens.
The IDS does not remediate the event; it detects it.

stem: Which statement MOST accurately compares application allowlisting and blocklisting?

options.text: Allowlisting denies by default and permits only approved software; blocklisting permits by default and blocks known-bad
options.rationale: Allowlisting's deny-by-default stance blocks unknown threats, whereas blocklisting only stops previously identified bad items.

options.text: Blocklisting is always more secure than allowlisting
options.rationale: Blocklisting cannot stop unknown malware, so it is generally weaker against novel threats than allowlisting.

options.text: Allowlisting permits everything except known-bad files
options.rationale: That description is blocklisting; allowlisting permits only what is explicitly approved.

options.text: The two approaches are functionally identical
options.rationale: They take opposite default postures (deny vs. permit), so they are not identical.

stem: Why do interactions with a properly deployed honeypot generate high-confidence alerts?

options.text: Because the honeypot has no legitimate use, so any access to it is inherently suspicious
options.rationale: Since no valid business traffic should touch a decoy, any interaction strongly indicates malicious or unauthorized activity.

options.text: Because honeypots block all attacks automatically
options.rationale: Honeypots detect and study; they do not block attacks.

options.text: Because honeypots are the organization's primary production servers
options.rationale: Honeypots are decoys, not production systems.

options.text: Because honeypots encrypt all network traffic
options.rationale: Encryption is not the purpose of a honeypot; detection through decoy interaction is.

stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of sandboxing a suspicious file?

options.text: To run it in isolation and safely observe its behavior
options.rationale: Sandboxing executes code in a contained environment so analysts can study malicious behavior without harming production.

options.text: To permanently store the file for archival
options.rationale: Sandboxing analyzes behavior; it is not an archival storage method.

options.text: To distribute the file to all endpoints
options.rationale: Distributing a suspicious file spreads risk rather than isolating it for analysis.

options.text: To sign the file as trusted
options.rationale: Sandboxing observes behavior; it does not sign or vouch for a file's trustworthiness.

stem: A prominent 'Premises under 24-hour video surveillance' sign is posted at an entrance. Which control function does the sign itself BEST represent, separate from the cameras?

options.rationale: The sign discourages would-be intruders before they act, which is a deterrent function distinct from the detective cameras.
The sign does not physically stop entry; it only discourages, making it deterrent, not preventive.
The sign does not remediate after an event.
The sign does not restore operations; it discourages beforehand.

stem: A legacy system cannot support the required multi-factor authentication. To satisfy the control objective, the team isolates it on a restricted segment with heavy monitoring. This alternative measure is BEST described as which type of control?

options.rationale: When the primary control (MFA) is not feasible, an alternative that meets the objective by other means is a compensating control.
Isolation and monitoring do more than discourage; they substitute for the infeasible control, which is compensating.
The measure is put in place proactively as a substitute, not to remediate after an event.
Recovery restores operations after an incident; this alternative substitutes for a missing preventive control.

stem: Endpoint software identifies a malicious executable and quarantines it. Which control functions does this software BEST combine?

options.text: Detective (identifying the malware) and corrective (removing/quarantining it)
options.rationale: Antivirus/EDR detects malicious code and then remediates it by quarantine or removal, spanning detective and corrective functions.

options.text: Only deterrent, since it discourages malware
options.rationale: The software actively identifies and removes malware rather than merely discouraging it.

options.text: Only physical, since it protects hardware
options.rationale: Antivirus is a logical control on software, not a physical control.

options.text: Only recovery, since it restores files
options.rationale: Its core role is detecting and removing malware, not restoring data like a backup.

stem: Which detection approach is LEAST likely to catch a brand-new zero-day attack for which no indicator exists yet?

options.rationale: Signature-based detection relies on known patterns and cannot match an attack for which no signature exists yet, making it least effective against zero-days.
Anomaly detection can flag unusual behavior even without a known signature, so it is more capable against zero-days.

options.text: A honeypot generating alerts on any interaction
options.rationale: A honeypot detects based on illegitimate interaction, not signatures, so it can catch novel activity.

options.text: UEBA flagging deviation from normal user behavior
options.rationale: Behavioral analytics can detect anomalies from novel attacks without predefined signatures.

stem: Management's stated goal is to 'stop unauthorized code from ever running,' not merely to detect it after the fact. Which control BEST matches this preventive goal?

options.rationale: Allowlisting prevents any unapproved code from executing at all, directly matching a preventive goal.
An IDS detects and alerts after activity occurs; it does not prevent code from running.
A honeypot detects and studies attackers; it does not prevent code execution on production endpoints.
A SIEM aggregates and correlates for detection, not prevention of code execution.
